documents.title: Water Rationing — Reduced Allocation
documents.location: All water pumps and the mess hall
documents.material: Printed on red paper (pre-war construction stock), hand-lettered
documents.transcript:
WATER RATIONING NOTICE
EFFECTIVE: Day 64

The water recycler membrane is degraded. Output has dropped by 20%. Until the replacement membrane is installed (estimated Day 67), daily water allocation is reduced:

FROM: 3 litres per person per day
TO: 2 litres per person per day

THIS INCLUDES:
- Drinking water
- Cooking water
- Hygiene water (washing, teeth)

THIS DOES NOT INCLUDE:
- Medical water (the infirmary has a separate reserve)
- Greenhouse water (the plants get their allocation from the condensate collector)

CONSERVATION TIPS:
- Fill your canteen once in the morning. That's your water for the day.
- Do not leave pumps running. Turn the handle off when your container is full.
- Report any leaks to the Plumber immediately. A dripping pipe wastes 4 litres per hour.

The replacement membrane is being fabricated now. Normal allocation will resume when it is installed. Thank you for your cooperation.

documents.title: Mediation Record — Dispute Between Dormitory B Residents
documents.material: Handwritten on standard form, filed in the mediation binder
documents.transcript:
MEDIATION RECORD — DAY 71
PARTIES: Resident M. (Bunk 14) and Resident K. (Bunk 15)
MEDIATOR: The Therapist

COMPLAINT: Resident M. reports that Resident K. is grinding their teeth at night, which prevents M. from sleeping. Resident K. reports that they are unaware of the grinding and cannot control it. Resident M. has requested a bunk change. Resident K. feels accused of a deliberate disturbance.

DISCUSSION:
- M. has not slept more than 3 consecutive hours in 9 days. Sleep deprivation is affecting their work performance and mood.
- K. grinds their teeth during stress-induced bruxism. This is a known symptom of chronic anxiety in enclosed environments. K. is not doing it on purpose.
- The dormitory walls are concrete. Sound travels. There is no privacy and no silence.

RESOLUTION:
1. K. will wear a boiled leather mouth guard at night (fabricated by the Tailor) to reduce the grinding noise.
2. M. will be offered ear plugs made from rolled cotton wool.
3. If neither measure works within 7 days, M. will be moved to Bunk 22 (currently unoccupied).
4. Both parties agree that this is not anyone's fault. The bunker is loud. The walls are thin. The stress is real.

FOLLOW-UP: Check in 7 days.

MEDIATOR'S NOTE: This is the fourth sleep-related dispute this month. The bunker needs a quiet room. I have proposed converting the sealed storage closet on Sub-Level 2 into a low-stimulus rest area. The Architect says it's possible. The Plumber says the ventilation can be isolated. Pending approval.

GREENHOUSE DUTY ROSTER
Week of Day 66

WATERING (daily, 07:00 and 17:00):
Mon — Suki
Tue — Botanist
Wed — Widow
Thu — Suki
Fri — Botanist
Sat — Teacher (children help)
Sun — Volunteer rotation

HARVESTING (as needed):
Wheat: check every 3 days. Harvest when heads are dry and golden.
Herbs: pick leaves, don't pull stems. Leave the root.
Turnips: ready at Day 75. All hands for harvest.

COMPOST TURNING (every 14 days):
Next due: Day 70 — Suki + Mechanic

SEED SAVING:
Wheat: select the 5 strongest heads. Do not eat them. They are next year's crop.
Herbs: let the flowers go to seed. Collect when dry.

NOTES:
- The greenhouse temperature must stay above 10°C at night. Check the stove.
- If the water recycler is down, use the condensate collector only. Do not use drinking water for plants.
- The children are not allowed to eat the wheat seedlings. This includes Petr. Yes, even Petr.
- If you see aphids, tell the Botanist immediately. Do not try to pick them off yourself.

documents.title: Medical Clinic — Hours and Availability
documents.material: Typed on recycled paper, laminated with salvaged plastic
documents.transcript:
INFIRMARY — CLINIC HOURS

ROUTINE CONSULTATIONS:
Mon/Wed/Fri: 09:00-11:00 and 15:00-17:00
Tue/Thu: 09:00-11:00 only

EMERGENCY CARE:
Available 24 hours. Knock on the infirmary door. If no answer, knock on the Surgeon's bunk (Sub-Level 1, Bunk 3).

MEDICATION DISPENSING:
By appointment only. The Pharmacist dispenses iodine, anti-rad, and antibiotics. Do not ask for more than your prescribed amount. The supply is finite.

DOSIMETER CALIBRATION:
Available Thu 14:00-16:00. Bring your dosimeter. Calibration takes 20 minutes.

MEDICAL SCREENING FOR NEW ARRIVALS:
All new arrivals must be screened before entry. This includes dosimeter reading, visual inspection for lesions, and a 6-hour quarantine in the decon adit. No exceptions.

THE SURGEON'S NOTE:
I am one person. I cannot fix everything. If you have a headache, drink water and rest. If you have a cut, clean it and bandage it. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, blood in your urine, or a fever above 38.5°C — come to the infirmary immediately. These are not things you can wait out.

Fri — Story time with the Historian (pre-war history for children)

MEALS:
Children eat at 07:00 (before adults), 12:00 (with adults), and 17:00 (before adults).
Children's portions are the same as adults. This is non-negotiable.

BEDTIME:
Lights out in the children's dormitory at 20:00.
The Therapist reads a story at 19:30. All children are welcome, including those who are not afraid of the dark.

NOTE FROM THE TEACHER:
If your child is not attending school, please let me know why. Some children are struggling with the enclosed environment. Some are grieving. Some are simply bored. I can help with all of these. But I need them in the schoolroom. A child who is not learning is a child who is forgetting what the world looks like. I am trying to help them remember.

documents.title: Radiation Safety Protocol — Surface Operations
documents.location: Main airlock and all surface access points
documents.transcript:
RADIATION SAFETY PROTOCOL — SURFACE OPERATIONS

BEFORE EXITING:
1. Check dosimeter. Record starting dose.
2. Put on gas mask. Check seal.
3. Put on outer clothing (coveralls, gloves, boots).
4. Note the time of exit.

DURING SURFACE OPERATIONS:
1. Check dosimeter every 30 minutes.
2. If dose rate exceeds 25 uSv/h, return immediately.
3. Maximum exposure time at 15 uSv/h: 4 hours.
4. Maximum exposure time at 25 uSv/h: 2 hours.
5. If ash storm begins, return immediately regardless of dose.

UPON RETURN:
1. Remove outer clothing in the airlock vestibule.
2. Shake off ash. Do not bring ash into the bunker.
3. Remove gas mask last.
4. Wash hands and face with soap and water.
5. Record final dosimeter reading.
6. Report to the Surgeon if dose exceeds 50 uSv in a single day.

WEEKLY DOSE LIMIT: 200 uSv. No exceptions.
MONTHLY DOSE LIMIT: 500 uSv. No exceptions.

IF YOU EXCEED A LIMIT:
- Report to the infirmary immediately
- Begin iodine protocol (1 pill immediately, 1 pill every 6 hours for 3 days)
- No further surface operations for 14 days
- The Surgeon will conduct a medical assessment

THE ASH DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOUR SCHEDULE. RESPECT THE DOSE.
